name: Exicom Tele-Systems Ltd
title: Exicom Tele-Systems Ltd - 544133 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Analyst / Investor Meet - Outcome

summary.headline: Exicom Q2 FY27 standalone revenue rose 21.3% YoY to ₹277 cr and consolidated EBITDA turned positive at ₹1.8 cr, while Tritium is being divested.
summary.overview: Standalone revenue reached ₹277 cr (up 21.3% YoY, 17% QoQ), with the EV charging segment crossing ₹100 cr for the first time at ₹206 cr (up 58.7% YoY). Standalone EBITDA rose to ₹25.6 cr at a 9.2% margin, and consolidated EBITDA swung to +₹1.8 cr from a ₹32.7 cr loss a year earlier. Consolidated PAT loss narrowed to ₹57.8 cr, held back by depreciation on the Hyderabad plant and Tritium amortisation. The board approved divesting 100% of Tritium, with a non-binding term sheet at an indicative enterprise value of $85 mn, targeted for December 2026 but possibly slipping.

segments.name: EV charging (standalone)
segments.commentary: Q2 revenue ₹206 cr, first quarter above ₹100 cr; H1 standalone EV revenue cited as ₹106 cr in one place and ₹167 cr in another, so the H1 figure is unclear in the transcript. Export mix about 10% in FY27.

segments.name: Critical power (standalone)
segments.commentary: Q2 revenue ₹271 cr, up 5.8% YoY. Bharatnet phase 3 visibility is ₹235 cr in FY27 and ₹478 cr in FY28, with the remainder in FY29.

segments.name: Tritium (subsidiary)
segments.commentary: Revenue up about 133% in the first nine months of calendar 2026 per management, with a record backlog contributing about 27% of consolidated revenue in H1 FY27. Q2 bookings were $14.7 mn against $17 mn in Q1, leaving a $23 mn backlog. Divestment at an indicative $85 mn EV is under negotiation.

segments.name: Battery energy storage (BESS)
segments.commentary: Focus on commercial and industrial and small office/home office. About 35 small projects (~10 MWh) executed, and the order book is three times that, about 30 MWh. Pilot-scale revenue this year is expected to scale to about ₹150 cr next year.

guidance_outlook: Order book of about ₹1,645 cr as of 30 September, giving revenue visibility of about ₹1,600 cr over the next 15 months; H1 FY27 order inflow about ₹377 cr with a book-to-bill of 0.73.
Management said FY28 growth is expected in both segments, but formal FY28 guidance will come before the end of FY27 (Q4 call), not on this call.
Export target of 30% of revenue within three years; exports expected to grow 3x in FY28 from the FY27 base, with 30-40% annual growth in export revenue.
Tritium divestment targeted for December 2026, but may spill into the next quarter. Management expects the deal to make Exicom net cash from net debt.
Tritium EBITDA break-even is expected sometime in the next financial year, with losses continuing during ramp-up. Two new Tritium products go into mass production in April and July 2027.
Service revenue of ₹40-50 cr over 10 years from certain telecom projects, starting in FY29.
capex_capacity: Over ₹200 cr of capex deployed in March 2026, with the Hyderabad (Adibatla) plant depreciation fully charged for the first time in Q2.
Gurgaon to Hyderabad transition described as substantially complete; production volumes normalising and inventory reduced to ₹36.6 cr.
Liquid-cooled power module line set up for Tritium at the Hyderabad facility; Exicom will keep manufacturing these modules for Tritium post-divestment.
Q2 FY27 EV volumes were about 90% higher than Q2 FY26, per management.
demand_pricing: EV market: management expects AC charger demand of about 12 lakh and DC charger demand of 25,000 through FY30. Working with 7 of the top 10 passenger vehicle OEMs and 17 of the top 20 CPOs.
Bus segment: more than 6,000 high-power chargers expected under PM e-Bus Sewa; truck segment about 1,000 chargers. Both are tender-based and cost-driven.
Telecom: demand of about 8 lakh lithium-ion batteries per year for 5G and tower companies. Management cited 5G subscribers rising from 25 cr to about 45 cr.
Margins: commodity, semiconductor and forex costs are rising. Unit-level margins were under pressure in Q2, offset by operating leverage at group level.
Customer mix: government direct business is under 5%. Top-five customer concentration is falling, and exports are about 10% of revenue.

qa_highlights.question: How much cash will reach Exicom from the Tritium sale after debt, leases and minority share, and will the investment be written down?
qa_highlights.answer: Management is still working through customary adjustments and gave no figure. It expects some compensation via power-module supply to Tritium and global monetisation of the EV charging tech.

qa_highlights.question: Why divest Tritium when it is approaching EBITDA break-even?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited the need for working capital and engineering investment to enter data-centre power infrastructure, plus higher capital needs for home-market and export growth. It called the decision difficult and said it was the best use of capital.

qa_highlights.question: Is the power-module manufacturing agreement exclusive, and what is its term and volume commitment?
qa_highlights.answer: Terms are not yet negotiated. Management said the module supply is unlikely to be exclusive, but it expects substantial revenue, and Tritium's volumes for the next three years are visible to it.

qa_highlights.question: Is there domestic guidance for FY28?
qa_highlights.answer: No formal guidance today. The ₹1,600 cr order book gives visibility, and guidance will come before the end of FY27 (Q4 results).

qa_highlights.question: How does Exicom differentiate in EV charging against new entrants?
qa_highlights.answer: It cites the full product range from 3.3 kW portable to high-power DC, high R&D spend, capacity of 1,000-3,000 chargers a month, quality and certification barriers for OEMs, and a service network in more than 200,000 locations.

qa_highlights.question: What are margins in EV charging versus telecom?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said unit-level margins were compressed by commodity, semiconductor and forex costs, but group EBITDA margin improved on operating leverage. No segment margin split was given.

risks_watch: Tritium divestment: the $85 mn indicative EV is non-binding, the net cash proceeds to Exicom are not yet computed, and the write-down risk is unquantified. Closing may slip past December 2026.
Consolidated PAT remains a loss of ₹57.8 cr, with high depreciation and Tritium amortisation still weighing on earnings.
Input cost pressure from commodities, semiconductors and forex, with partial pass-through to customers.
Tender-based bus and truck segments are cost-driven and highly competitive, and new EV charging entrants are increasing competition.
Export ramp-up (30% target in three years) and BESS scale-up (about ₹150 cr next year) are unproven at scale.
Bharatnet execution timing may shift revenue from FY28 to FY29.
summary.management_tone: Confident on the standalone turnaround and operating leverage, with the EV charging growth framed as a key driver. Noticeably guarded on Tritium: the transaction terms, cash proceeds and the closing date were left open, and the call gave no FY28 numeric guidance.
key_quotes: This quarter your company delivered a turnaround result both in terms of standalone and consolidated performance.
Consolidated EBITDA has turned positive at 1.8 crores swinging from the 32.7 crore loss in the same quarter and last year.
we have received a non-binding term sheet for 100 percent of the tritium group at an indicative valuation of 85 million dollars on a cash free and debt free basis

growth.why: No numeric FY27 revenue guidance; FY28 growth flagged in both segments with formal guidance deferred to Q4 call, backed by order book of about Rs 1,645 cr (~Rs 1,600 cr visibility over 15 months), though H1 book-to-bill was only 0.73 and Q2 standalone revenue grew 21.3% YoY.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Standalone EBITDA margin rose to 9.2% from 6.6% YoY and consolidated EBITDA turned to +₹1.8 cr, driven by operating leverage, though unit-level EV margins were compressed by commodity, semiconductor and forex costs.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Hyderabad (Adibatla) plant commissioned after over ₹200 cr capex deployed in March 2026, with depreciation fully charged from Q2; Gurgaon-to-Hyderabad transition substantially complete.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: EV volumes about 90% higher YoY in Q2 and EV revenue up 58.7% to ₹206 cr standalone; order book ~₹1,645 cr gives ~₹1,600 cr visibility over 15 months, though H1 book-to-bill was only 0.73.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Capex was not discussed beyond the ₹200 cr already deployed in March 2026 and the Tritium liquid-cooled module line; no utilisation figure was given and no new plant was announced.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: No numeric FY27 or FY28 guidance was given on this call; formal FY28 guidance is deferred to the Q4 FY27 call, so no upgrade is signalled.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Bharatnet phase 3 timing may shift revenue from FY28 to FY29 (₹478 cr planned in FY28), and consolidated PAT remains a ₹57.8 cr loss with input-cost pressure.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Two new Tritium products are scheduled for mass production in April and July 2027, and BESS pilot revenue is set to scale to about ₹150 cr next year.

rows.label: Tritium divestment at indicative $85 mn EV
rows.when: Dec 2026, may slip into next quarter
rows.why: Board approved 100% sale with a non-binding term sheet; management expects the deal to make Exicom net cash from net debt, but cash proceeds and write-down are not yet quantified.

rows.label: Export ramp to 30% of revenue
rows.why: Exports are about 10% of revenue today and management targets 30-40% annual export growth, but this is unproven at scale.

rows.label: Bharatnet phase 3 revenue
rows.why: Bharatnet phase 3 visibility is ₹235 cr in FY27 and ₹478 cr in FY28, with the remainder in FY29, though execution timing may shift.

tone.note: Management was confident on the standalone turnaround, EV growth and operating leverage, but guarded on Tritium's terms, cash proceeds, closing date and write-down; analysts pushed on Tritium's cash and exclusivity and on the lack of FY28 numeric guidance.
